findings.reason: The protected source is already the standard robust codec: emit decimal length, `#`, and payload for each string; then parse one header and exactly its declared payload at a time. Content never needs escaping, the cursor invariant is direct, the app adapter exposes both native operations cleanly, and no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies paid-only LeetCode problem 271 and its Python Codec interface plus offline operation adapter. The Reference preserves sender/receiver semantics, exact ordered reconstruction, serialization prohibition, both examples, all three source constraints, and the arbitrary-character-set follow-up; the contract now defines c for both operations.

The immutable native Codec is tied to verified submission 2064297848. Its field format, generator assembly, cursor, separator search, length parse, payload slice, cursor advance, and result match the app-local Codec exactly; the app-only `solve` dispatcher is the permitted contract adapter.

The previous largest benchmark illegally encoded 256 strings against the 200-string source limit. The replacement 16/64/200-string tiers use legal maximum-length ASCII payloads and span 3,200/12,800/40,000 payload characters. The current source passes at -0.03 relative exponent and 0.95x largest ratio; a correct encoder that rebuilds every accumulated prefix passes all outputs but fails only scaling at +1.25 and 57.31x.

The Approach now describes the protected length-prefix codec exactly, removes corrupted punctuation, defines the cursor invariant and both linear passes, accounts for returned-space usage, and separates sentinel, escaping, empty-value, and arbitrary-character considerations.

The hash-bound paid-only Reference remains source-fidelity verified with both examples, all three constraints, and the follow-up intact. Its one source transmission diagram is now represented by one accessible Mermaid flow with the same sender-message-receiver relationship and passes the Mermaid gate.
